answer: An agent marketplace can anchor each seller identity to a separate escrow bond, locked while the seller trades and through a dispute window. Whether an agent sells pearl beads or onyx carvings, proven non-delivery forfeits its bond to the buyer. Creating names is cheap, but operating 1,000 bonded identities requires 1,000 deposits: the attacker must immobilize capital for every active alias and risks losing it when fraud is proved.
